trick: Implantation happens at the BLASTOCYST stage, not the morula. The order is zygote → cleavage → morula (a solid ball, still in the fallopian tube) → blastocyst (hollow, with a trophoblast) → implantation in the uterine wall. Only the blastocyst has the trophoblast that can attach, which is why the morula cannot implant.

data.prompt: Put the stages from fertilisation to implantation in the right order.

items.label: Fertilisation
items.note: Sperm meets ovum in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube

items.label: Zygote
items.note: The single diploid cell formed by fusion

items.label: Cleavage
items.note: Rapid mitotic divisions with no growth between them, still inside the tube

items.label: Morula
items.note: A solid ball of 8 to 16 blastomeres — cannot implant

items.label: Blastocyst
items.note: Hollow, with an inner cell mass and an outer trophoblast

items.label: Implantation
items.note: The trophoblast attaches to the uterine endometrium — this is the stage that implants

trick: A monohybrid cross gives 3:1 phenotypic but 1:2:1 genotypic — quoting the wrong one is the commonest error. A dihybrid gives 9:3:3:1, and a test cross with a recessive parent gives 1:1. Learn the four ratios as a set, and read carefully whether the question asks for phenotype or genotype.

video.query: mendel monohybrid dihybrid cross ratios linkage class 12 biology

data.prompt: Work a monohybrid cross through to the ratios.
data.problem: A tall pea plant homozygous for tallness (TT) is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). Tallness is dominant.

steps.ask: What is the genotype of every F₁ plant?
steps.why: Each parent contributes one allele: T from the tall parent, t from the dwarf. All F₁ are heterozygous.

steps.ask: What does the F₁ generation look like?
steps.why: T is dominant, so a single copy makes the plant tall. The dwarf character is hidden, not lost.

steps.ask: Selfing the F₁, what is the phenotypic ratio in F₂?
steps.why: TT, Tt, Tt and tt — three plants show tallness to one dwarf.

steps.ask: And the genotypic ratio in F₂?
steps.why: One TT, two Tt, one tt. The phenotypic and genotypic ratios are different, and questions rely on that.

steps.ask: Crossing an F₁ plant with a dwarf (a test cross) gives what ratio?
steps.why: Tt × tt gives half Tt and half tt — this is exactly how a test cross reveals whether a tall plant is TT or Tt.

data.answer: F₁ all Tt and tall; F₂ 3:1 by phenotype but 1:2:1 by genotype; a test cross gives 1:1.

trick: Replication makes DNA from DNA, transcription makes RNA from DNA, translation makes protein from RNA — the central dogma in three words, and each question names one of them. Chargaff's rule (A = T, G = C) applies to double-stranded DNA only, so it does not hold for RNA or for single-stranded viral DNA.

trick: Match the structure to the argument it supports. Homologous organs — same origin, different function — argue for divergent evolution from a common ancestor; analogous organs — different origin, same function — argue for convergent evolution. The wing of a bat and the arm of a man are homologous; the wing of a bat and the wing of a butterfly are analogous.

trick: Restriction enzymes cut, ligase joins, and the vector carries — three tools, three verbs, and every recombinant DNA question uses them in that order. EcoRI cuts at a palindromic sequence leaving sticky ends, which is exactly why the fragment and the plasmid fit together.

data.prompt: Put the steps of making recombinant DNA in order.

items.label: Isolation of the DNA
items.note: The gene of interest and the vector DNA are obtained in pure form

items.label: Cutting with a restriction enzyme
items.note: The same enzyme cuts both, leaving matching sticky ends

items.label: Ligation
items.note: DNA ligase seals the fragment into the vector, forming recombinant DNA

items.label: Transformation into a host
items.note: The recombinant vector is introduced into a bacterial cell

items.label: Selection of transformants
items.note: Marker genes reveal which cells took up the construct

items.label: Culture and product recovery
